newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's RCTI says ready to float shares.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's RCTI says ready to float shares.

text.p: Indonesia's largest privately-owned television station Rajawali Citra Televisi Indonesia (RCTI), a unit of conglomerate Bimantara Citra, said on Tuesday it was ready to float its shares this year.
"Parliament approved the broadcasting bill (last year). Now we are waiting for the signing by President Suharto," Ralie Siregar, RCTI's president-director, told analysts.
"As soon as the president signs the bill, we are ready to go public....If it is signed this year, we are ready this year," he added.
Siregar, who gave no other details, was speaking to analysts in a meeting organised by Ing Barings Securities Indonesia.
Parliament passed Indonesia's first broadcasting bill last year. Suharto must sign the bill into law but no date has been set.
RCTI had earlier expected to list its shares on the local stock exchange but the previous regulations did not allow the company to do so. The new bill will allow RCTI to go public.

Siregar said the firm's advertising revenue was expected to rise to 360 billion rupiah in 1997 against 300 billion rupiah in 1996. He said most of RCTI's advertising revenues came from the pharmaceutical, food and automotive sectors.
Bimantara's broadcasting and media division contributed 33.5 percent or 39.5 billion rupiah of the company's net profit in 1995 against 41.26 percent or 19.6 billion rupiah in 1994.
